issues.description: Delimiter lookup table conflates the API with its data
issues.detail: The _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict maps each literal character to itself ({',': ',', '|': '|', ' ': ' '}) alongside the two symbolic names. Data dominates: a cleaner shape is a set of allowed chars plus a small alias dict ({'pipeDelimited': '|', 'spaceDelimited': ' '}), then resolve via `delim = aliases.get(delimiter, delimiter); if delim not in allowed: raise`. Same behavior, less redundancy, the algorithm becomes obvious.

issues.description: Validation happens inside the hot path instead of once at call boundary
issues.detail: The unsupported-delimiter check runs on every request that hits this branch, even though the set of valid delimiters is fixed at import time. It is cheap, but the shape is wrong: validation of a constant-domain argument belongs at the top of the function (before the params lookup) so the error is raised consistently whether or not the param happens to be present. Right now passing delimiter=';' with a missing param silently returns the default; with a present param it raises ValueError. Same input, different outcome depending on unrelated state.

issues.description: Six overloads added solely to thread one optional kwarg through
issues.detail: Each of the six get_param_as_list overloads grew a `delimiter: str | None = None` line. This is a Python typing constraint, not a design smell of this PR per se, but it is worth noting that the overload set is now carrying real maintenance weight; any future kwarg multiplies it again. Not blocking, but a signal that the data structure (the signature) is fighting the algorithm (the dispatch). Leave alone for now.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE overall. The change is a stateless transform — input string, output list — bolted onto an existing method with minimal surface area. The core logic is four lines and reads cleanly. Two small data-shape nits: the delimiter table redundantly maps characters to themselves when an aliases-plus-allowed-set shape would be more honest, and validation of a constant-domain argument should happen at the call boundary rather than inside the conditional branch where it can be skipped when the param is absent. The six-overload expansion is noise but not this PR's fault. Tests cover the obvious cases including the auto_parse_qs_csv interaction and the explode/multi-value case. No blockers.
